Dear Dr. Chen,

Thank you for seeing Maya Patel, an active 3-year-old girl who presents for specialized assessment. Her issues began during the first week of life when she required phototherapy in the newborn nursery, and she has had persistent hematologic abnormalities since that time.

On physical examination today, Maya is bright, interactive, and meeting all cognitive and motor milestones. Her heart sounds are normal, and her lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. She does, however, exhibit mild yellowing of her skin along with notable yellowing of the conjunctival tissue. Her abdomen is soft and non-tender, but her liver margin is palpable 3 cm beneath the right costal margin, and a firm spleen tip is easily felt 2.5 cm below the left costal margin.

Her most recent complete blood count shows a low hemoglobin of 8.6 g/dL accompanied by an elevated reticulocyte index of 7.2%. Review of the peripheral blood smear reveals prominent oval and elongated pencil-shaped red cells. Direct antiglobulin testing has been consistently negative, and her G6PD enzyme levels were well within normal limits. Furthermore, hemoglobin studies showed no evidence of uneven or disproportionate globin chain production.

Maya lives with both parents and takes a standard over-the-counter multivitamin. There is no family history of early-onset jaundice, gallstones, or splenectomy. 

I would appreciate your expert opinion regarding these findings and your advice on the best management strategy moving forward. 

Warm regards,

Dr. Sarah Miller
Oakridge Pediatric Clinic
